question: Assume today is 2026-09-10. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the total container volume handled by the Port of Los Angeles in September 2026, in TEUs (twenty-foot equivalent units; loaded and empty imports and exports combined), as it will be first reported in the Port of Los Angeles's monthly cargo news release.

target.what: Total container volume handled by the Port of Los Angeles (loaded + empty, imports + exports combined) during September 2026, as first reported in the Port's monthly cargo news release
target.publisher: Port of Los Angeles (Port of Los Angeles monthly cargo news release / TEU statistics)
target.caveats: Target period is future/ongoing relative to the 2026-09-10 cutoff; September 2026 is only ~1/3 elapsed at cutoff, so most of the month must be projected. Definition is total TEU (loaded imports + loaded exports + empty imports + empty exports), matching the Port's headline 'total TEU' figure. Altern

methods.rationale: Year-over-year route anchored on the same month last year, adjusted by a small drift factor informed by 2026 cumulative +1.8% but July -6% and national imports turning negative. Shared dependency: relies on the September 2025 base being comparable in definition (total TEU, loaded+empty).

a2.role: September/August seasonal ratio applied as a proxy for September/July level

methods.rationale: Level route from the latest observed month (July 2026, 960,464 TEU) times a September/August seasonal ratio. Because August 2026 is unpublished at cutoff, the ratio is applied to July as a proxy; this is a weaker route than m1 and its failure mode is that July-to-September differs from August-to-September.

Naive seasonal benchmark: average of the two most recent September totals (2025 and 2024). Provides a no-drift baseline against which the adjusted routes can be compared; it ignores the 2026 trend and is expected to be a weak but unbiased anchor.

assumptions.name: September 2026 vs September 2025 total TEU change factor
assumptions.rationale: LA's 2026 cumulative is +1.8% YoY through July, but July was -6% YoY and Global Port Tracker shows national imports turning negative by August 2026 (-4.5%). September 2025 was already a weak month (-7.5% YoY), so a near-flat to slightly negative YoY factor is plausible; range spans a modest recovery to a sharper tariff-driven decline.
assumptions.applies_when: LA September 2026 tracks its own September 2025 base with a small YoY drift consistent with mid-2026 trends.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence of a sharp September 2026 surge or collapse (e.g., a new tariff deadline front-loading or a port disruption) that moves YoY well outside the range.

assumptions.name: September/August seasonal ratio for LA total TEU
assumptions.rationale: In 2025 September/August was 883,053/958,355 ≈ 0.92; in 2024 September was a record and roughly flat to August. A ratio near 0.92 with a range down to 0.85 reflects the typical autumn decline after the summer peak.
assumptions.applies_when: September 2026 follows the normal post-summer seasonal decline from the August level.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that September 2026 is unusually strong (e.g., holiday front-loading) or unusually weak relative to August.

methods.label: m1

p1.role: Port of LA total TEU, September 2025

methods.rationale: Year-over-year route anchored on the same month last year, adjusted by a small drift factor informed by 2026 cumulative +1.8% but July -6% and national imports turning negative. Shared dependency: relies on the September 2025 base being comparable in definition (total TEU, loaded+empty).

methods.label: m3
methods.rationale: Naive seasonal benchmark: average of the two most recent September totals (2025 and 2024). Provides a no-drift baseline against which the adjusted routes can be compared; it ignores the 2026 trend and is expected to be a weak but unbiased anchor.

excluded_by_input_audit.label: m2
excluded_by_input_audit.reason: input audit: a2: The assumption is a September/August seasonal ratio, but it is applied to a July base; the ratio's denominator period (August) does not match the base period (July).

kept.name: September 2026 vs September 2025 total TEU change factor
kept.rationale: LA's 2026 cumulative is +1.8% YoY through July, but July was -6% YoY and Global Port Tracker shows national imports turning negative by August 2026 (-4.5%). September 2025 was already a weak month (-7.5% YoY), so a near-flat to slightly negative YoY factor is plausible; range spans a modest recovery
kept.applies_when: LA September 2026 tracks its own September 2025 base with a small YoY drift consistent with mid-2026 trends.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence of a sharp September 2026 surge or collapse (e.g., a new tariff deadline front-loading or a port disruption) that moves YoY well outside the range.

kept.name: September/August seasonal ratio for LA total TEU
kept.rationale: In 2025 September/August was 883,053/958,355 ≈ 0.92; in 2024 September was a record and roughly flat to August. A ratio near 0.92 with a range down to 0.85 reflects the typical autumn decline after the summer peak.
kept.applies_when: September 2026 follows the normal post-summer seasonal decline from the August level.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence that September 2026 is unusually strong (e.g., holiday front-loading) or unusually weak relative to August.

The best computed estimate for total container volume handled by the Port of Los Angeles (loaded plus empty, imports plus exports combined) during September 2026 is 886,499 TEU (80% model-based interval 643,481 to 1,221,296 TEU). This is a projection: September 2026 was only partly elapsed at the cutoff, so most of the month is forecast.

Two methods were combined at 50% and 50% weight. The first applies an assumed year-over-year factor of 0.97 (range 0.85 to 1.1) to the observed September 2025 total of 883,053 TEU, giving 855,260 TEU. The second is a naive seasonal average of the two most recent Septembers, 883,053 TEU and 954,706 TEU, giving 918,880 TEU. Only those observed points are data; the drift factor is an assumption.

The main risk is that the assumed factor is wrong, since 2026 trends were mixed. Actual September 2026 daily throughput data would most improve the estimate.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
